library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yoshida_2020_crenezumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yoshida_2020_crenezumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1186/s13195-020-0580-2> (open access)

Crenezumab is a humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds monomeric and
aggregated amyloid-beta (Abeta). Yoshida et al. pooled serum crenezumab and
plasma total (free + bound) monomeric Abeta(1-40) and Abeta(1-42) from three
trials and fitted a target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model with the
Michaelis-Menten approximation (their Figure 1). Crenezumab follows
two-compartment kinetics with first-order SC absorption. Each Abeta species is
a turnover pool with zero-order synthesis and its own peripheral distribution
compartment. The Abeta pool is split algebraically into a free fraction
`Kd / (Kd + Ccren)`, degraded at `Kdeg`, and a crenezumab-bound fraction
`Ccren / (Kd + Ccren)`, eliminated at `kint = CLint / Vcent`. Because the
complex is cleared about 300-800 times more slowly than free Abeta, total
plasma Abeta rises after dosing until it reaches a plateau.

The paper also reports CSF crenezumab and CSF Abeta(1-42) descriptively. Those
data were not modelled and have no counterpart here.

# Population

The analysis included 131 crenezumab-treated patients with mild-to-moderate
Alzheimer's disease from the phase II ABBY (NCT01343966; Abeta data from the
safety run-in cohort only) and BLAZE (NCT01397578) studies and the phase Ib
GN29632 study (NCT02353598). Together they contributed 1332 serum PK and 2203
plasma PD samples (Methods; Table 1). The regimens were 300 mg SC every 2 weeks
and 15, 30, 45, 60 or 120 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks. The studies enrolled patients
aged 50-80 (phase II) or 50-90 (phase Ib) years. The paper prints no
demographics table. The covariate analysis gives the 90% observed ranges as
52.4-95.9 kg for body weight, 54-82 years for age and 46.5-94.0
mL/min/1.73 m^2 for GFR. Its typical patient (Figure 7) is a 72-year-old male
weighing 72.3 kg with a GFR of 72.5 mL/min/1.73 m^2.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Yoshida_2020_crenezumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. They are
collected here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CLel) | 0.159 L/day | Table 2 |
| `lclint` (CLint) | 1.01 L/day | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (Vcent) | 2.89 L | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (crenezumab Vperiph) | 1.84 L | Table 2 |
| `lq` (crenezumab Q) | 0.142 L/day | Table 2 |
| `lfdepot` (Fsc) | 66.2% | Table 2 |
| `lka` (Ka) | 0.161 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lkd_ab40`, `lkd_ab42` | 12.0, 9.37 nM | Table 2 |
| `lrbase_ab40`, `lrbase_ab42` | 142, 5.98 pM | Table 2; Results text |
| `lkdeg_ab40`, `lkdeg_ab42` | 114, 287 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lq_ab40`, `lvp_ab40` | 8.72 L/day, 3.77 L | Table 2 |
| `lq_ab42`, `lvp_ab42` | 229 L/day, 8.19 L | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_clint`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.835, 0.474, 0.725 | Table 2 (power form, footnote) |
| `e_age_rbase_ab40` | 0.0037 1/year | Table 2 (linear form) |
| `e_crcl_rbase_ab40`, `e_crcl_rbase_ab42` | -0.0035, -0.0048 | Table 2 (linear form) |
| `e_sex_kdeg` | -0.16 (male), shared | Table 2, footnote b |
| Covariate reference values 72.3 kg, 72 years, 72.5 mL/min/1.73 m^2 | -- | Figure 7 legend (typical patient) |
| IIV (`etalcl`, `etalclint`, `etalvc`, `etalvp`) | 19.1, 15.3, 18.3, 75.2 CV% | Table 2 |
| IIV `etalkd`, `etalkdeg` (one eta each, shared by both species) | 13.6, 17.9 CV% | Table 2, footnote a |
| IIV `etalrbase_ab40`, `etalrbase_ab42` | 8.3, 13.8 CV% | Table 2 |
| `mw` | 150000 g/mol | not in paper (nominal IgG) |
| Residual error | fixed to 0 | not reported |
| Michaelis-Menten target-mediated elimination `kint * A * C / (Kd + C)` | -- | Figure 1 |
| Free-Abeta degradation `kdeg * A * Kd / (Kd + C)` | -- | Figure 1 |
| Depot, central, peripheral crenezumab; Abeta synthesis and peripheral distribution | -- | Figure 1 |

# Model

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Yoshida_2020_crenezumab")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical patient of Figure 7
typical_cov <- data.frame(WT = 72.3, AGE = 72, CRCL = 72.5, SEXF = 0)
```

The model has three outputs: `Cc`, serum crenezumab in ug/mL, and `Ctotal_ab40`
and `Ctotal_ab42`, total plasma Abeta in pM. It also returns the model-inferred
free Abeta (`Cfree_ab40`, `Cfree_ab42`) and crenezumab in nM (`Cc_nM`).
Observation rows name the ODE state `central` and carry `dvid = 1`; rxode2
returns every output column on each observation row.

```{r helpers}
# One subject per row of `cov`, IV doses (mg/kg, 60-min infusion) or SC doses
# (mg) at `dose_times`, observations at `obs_times`.
make_events <- function(cov, dose_mgkg = NA, dose_sc_mg = NA, dose_times,
                        obs_times, id_offset = 0L) {
  cov$id <- seq_len(nrow(cov)) + id_offset
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      evid = 1L,
      cmt = if (is.na(dose_sc_mg)) "central" else "depot",
      amt = if (is.na(dose_sc_mg)) dose_mgkg * WT else dose_sc_mg,
      dur = if (is.na(dose_sc_mg)) 1 / 24 else 0,
      dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, dur = 0, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

# Baseline Abeta and covariate effects (Figure 7, right column)

The steady-state baseline is the Table 2 value scaled by the linear age and GFR
terms. This check confirms the centering: at 72 years and GFR 72.5 the
baselines are exactly 142 and 5.98 pM. The Figure 7 bars were digitised by the
maintainers.

```{r baseline}
fig7_cov <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,    ~AGE, ~CRCL, ~ab40_fig7, ~ab42_fig7,
  "Typical",      72,  72.5,      142,      5.98,
  "Age 54",       54,  72.5,      133,      5.98,
  "Age 82",       82,  72.5,      147,      5.98,
  "GFR 94.0",     72,  94.0,      131,      5.40,
  "GFR 46.5",     72,  46.5,      155,      6.75
)
ev_base <- fig7_cov |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 72.3, SEXF = 0, id = dplyr::row_number(), time = 0,
                evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, dvid = 1L)
base <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev_base, keep = "scenario") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, Ctotal_ab40, Ctotal_ab42) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig7_cov, by = "scenario")

base |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Abeta(1-40) model (pM)" = round(Ctotal_ab40, 1),
    "Abeta(1-40) Figure 7 (pM)" = ab40_fig7,
    "Abeta(1-42) model (pM)" = round(Ctotal_ab42, 2),
    "Abeta(1-42) Figure 7 (pM)" = ab42_fig7
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Deterministic (no IIV): the only differences are digitisation error.
stopifnot(
  abs(base$Ctotal_ab40[1] - 142) < 1e-6,
  abs(base$Ctotal_ab42[1] - 5.98) < 1e-6,
  all(abs(base$Ctotal_ab40 / base$ab40_fig7 - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(base$Ctotal_ab42 / base$ab42_fig7 - 1) < 0.03)
)
```

The paper reports that over 90% of the observed GFR range, baselines differ
1.2-fold (Abeta(1-40)) and 1.25-fold (Abeta(1-42)), and that over the age range
Abeta(1-40) differs 1.1-fold. The model gives
`r round(base$Ctotal_ab40[5] / base$Ctotal_ab40[4], 2)`,
`r round(base$Ctotal_ab42[5] / base$Ctotal_ab42[4], 2)` and
`r round(base$Ctotal_ab40[3] / base$Ctotal_ab40[2], 2)`.

# Crenezumab PK after the first IV dose (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows mean serum crenezumab over the first 28 days. Its y-axis is
labelled ng/mL, but the values (about 3000 at 120 mg/kg, which is 8.7 g in
2.89 L) are in ug/mL. The means below were digitised by the maintainers. The
15 mg/kg arm came from ABBY/BLAZE and the other arms from GN29632.

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Yoshida 2020: typical-patient serum crenezumab after a single IV dose (lines) with the published means (points)."}
fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~time, ~conc,
  15, 0, 285, 15, 1, 265, 15, 7, 150, 15, 14, 100, 15, 28, 60,
  30, 0, 760, 30, 1, 650, 30, 7, 350, 30, 14, 270, 30, 28, 120,
  45, 0, 1230, 45, 1, 1040, 45, 7, 550, 45, 14, 400, 45, 28, 180,
  60, 0, 1570, 60, 1, 1300, 60, 7, 700, 60, 14, 520, 60, 28, 350,
  120, 0, 3150, 120, 1, 2760, 120, 7, 1600, 120, 14, 940, 120, 28, 650
)
doses_iv <- c(15, 30, 45, 60, 120)
# Published "day 0" samples were drawn ~60 min after the end of the infusion.
obs_sd <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.25), 2 / 24, 1, 7, 14, 28)))
ev_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_iv), function(i) {
  make_events(typical_cov, dose_mgkg = doses_iv[i], dose_times = 0,
              obs_times = obs_sd, id_offset = i - 1L) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = doses_iv[i])
}))
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev_sd, keep = "dose") |> as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_sd, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig2, aes(time, conc)) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Serum crenezumab (ug/mL)", colour = "mg/kg") +
  theme_bw()

cmp_fig2 <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = ifelse(abs(time - 2 / 24) < 1e-9, 0, time)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 1, 7, 14, 28), !(time == 0 & Cc == 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(dose, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2, by = c("dose", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc / conc - 1))
cmp_fig2 |>
  dplyr::transmute("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Day" = time,
                   "Model (ug/mL)" = signif(Cc, 3), "Figure 2 mean (ug/mL)" = conc,
                   "Difference (%)" = round(pct_diff)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The GN29632 arms (30-120 mg/kg) agree with the published means. The median
difference is `r round(median(cmp_fig2$pct_diff[cmp_fig2$dose > 15]))`%. The
15 mg/kg means sit below dose-proportionality in the data themselves: the day-0
mean is 19 ug/mL per mg/kg, against 25-27 for the other arms. The model, which
is dose-proportional, therefore runs above that arm.

```{r fig2-check}
# Typical patient vs digitised means of 9-21 patients: assert on the centre.
stopifnot(abs(median(cmp_fig2$pct_diff[cmp_fig2$dose > 15])) < 15)
```

The paper quotes a half-life of about 20 days for CLel and Vcent. That equals
`log(2) * (Vcent + Vperiph) / CLel` =
`r round(log(2) * (2.89 + 1.84) / 0.159, 1)` days. The terminal disposition
half-life of the two-compartment model is longer:
`r {k10 <- 0.159/2.89; k12 <- 0.142/2.89; k21 <- 0.142/1.84; a <- k10 + k12 + k21; round(log(2) / ((a - sqrt(a^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2), 1)}` days.
The paper's Discussion gives the complex elimination rate as 0.36 /day. The
model's `kint = CLint / Vcent` is `r round(1.01 / 2.89, 3)` /day.

# Total plasma Abeta after the first IV dose (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows mean total Abeta in the first 28 days. Its printed y-axis is
ng/mL. It is internally inconsistent with Figure 4, which plots the same
GN29632 week-5 trough samples in nM. For example, 120 mg/kg on day 28 is about
56 ng/mL (13 nM for Abeta(1-40), MW about 4330 g/mol) in Figure 3, but about
20-25 nM in Figure 4. The Table 2 baselines and the Figure 4 plateaus agree
with the model, so Figure 3 is compared on **shape** only. Each profile is
normalised to its own day-7 value, which cancels the absolute scale.

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates the shape of Figure 3 of Yoshida 2020: total plasma Abeta normalised to the day-7 value, typical patient (lines) vs published means (points)."}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~species, ~dose, ~d1, ~d7, ~d14, ~d28,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 15, 14.5, 28, 22, 11,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 30, 16, 43, 37.5, 19.5,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 45, 15, 47.5, 43, 26,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 60, 15.5, 50, 54, 37,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 120, 15, 57, 64.5, 56,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 15, 0.95, 1.75, 1.37, 0.73,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 30, 1.0, 2.5, 2.1, 1.18,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 45, 1.0, 2.55, 2.27, 1.45,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 60, 1.0, 3.0, 3.02, 2.12,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 120, 0.95, 3.35, 3.7, 3.07
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(d1:d28, names_to = "day", values_to = "obs") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = as.numeric(sub("d", "", day))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(species, dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(obs_rel = obs / obs[time == 7]) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

sim_ab <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::select(dose, time, Ctotal_ab40, Ctotal_ab42) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Ctotal_ab40, Ctotal_ab42), names_to = "species", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(species = ifelse(species == "Ctotal_ab40", "Abeta(1-40)", "Abeta(1-42)")) |>
  dplyr::distinct(species, dose, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::group_by(species, dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rel = conc / conc[time == 7]) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

ggplot(sim_ab, aes(time, rel, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3, aes(time, obs_rel)) +
  facet_wrap(~species) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Total Abeta / day-7 value", colour = "mg/kg") +
  theme_bw()

cmp_fig3 <- sim_ab |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(1, 14, 28)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig3, by = c("species", "dose", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (rel / obs_rel - 1))
cmp_fig3 |>
  dplyr::transmute("Species" = species, "Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Day" = time,
                   "Model (rel. day 7)" = round(rel, 2),
                   "Figure 3 (rel. day 7)" = round(obs_rel, 2),
                   "Difference (%)" = round(pct_diff)) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp_fig3$pct_diff)) < 15,
  quantile(abs(cmp_fig3$pct_diff), 0.75) < 40
)
```

The model reproduces the dose-dependent shape. At 15 mg/kg total Abeta peaks
near day 7 and falls by day 14. At 120 mg/kg it is still rising at day 14 and
stays high at day 28. Day 1 for Abeta(1-42) is the least well matched point.
Relative to day 7, the model's day-1 value is 20-33% below the published
mean; for Abeta(1-40) day 1 matches to within 10%.

# Trough total Abeta vs trough crenezumab (Figure 4)

Figure 4 plots trough total plasma Abeta against trough serum crenezumab (both
in nM) at weeks 5, 9 and 13, with the model median and 5-95% prediction
interval. The virtual cohort below approximates the trial population: body
weight log-normal with median 72.3 kg and 90% range 52.4-95.9 kg; age normal
with mean 72 years and 90% range 54-82; GFR normal with mean 72.5 and 90% range
46.5-94.0 mL/min/1.73 m^2; 50% female (not reported). Each arm has 100
patients.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20200121)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200121)
make_cov <- function(n) {
  data.frame(
    WT = exp(rnorm(n, log(72.3), (log(95.9) - log(52.4)) / (2 * 1.645))),
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 72, (82 - 54) / (2 * 1.645)), 50), 90),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 72.5, (94 - 46.5) / (2 * 1.645)), 20), 130),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  )
}
n_arm <- 100
arms <- list(
  list(label = "300 mg SC q2w", mgkg = NA, sc = 300, ii = 14),
  list(label = "15 mg/kg q4w", mgkg = 15, sc = NA, ii = 28),
  list(label = "30 mg/kg q4w", mgkg = 30, sc = NA, ii = 28),
  list(label = "45 mg/kg q4w", mgkg = 45, sc = NA, ii = 28),
  list(label = "60 mg/kg q4w", mgkg = 60, sc = NA, ii = 28),
  list(label = "120 mg/kg q4w", mgkg = 120, sc = NA, ii = 28)
)
ev_trough <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arms), function(i) {
  a <- arms[[i]]
  make_events(make_cov(n_arm), dose_mgkg = a$mgkg, dose_sc_mg = a$sc,
              dose_times = seq(0, 83, by = a$ii),
              obs_times = c(28, 56, 84) - 1e-3,
              id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_arm) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = a$label)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_trough[ev_trough$evid == 0, c("id", "time")])))
sim_trough <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_trough, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = sapply(arms, `[[`, "label")))
```

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Yoshida 2020: trough total Abeta vs trough crenezumab at weeks 5, 9 and 13 (points: simulated patients); line and band: binned median and 5-95% interval of the simulation; crosses: model median line digitised from Figure 4."}
fig4_line <- tibble::tribble(
  ~species, ~cren_nM, ~ab_nM,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 1000, 8, "Abeta(1-40)", 2500, 17, "Abeta(1-40)", 5000, 25,
  "Abeta(1-40)", 7500, 28.5, "Abeta(1-40)", 10000, 29,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 1000, 0.6, "Abeta(1-42)", 2500, 1.35, "Abeta(1-42)", 5000, 2.0,
  "Abeta(1-42)", 7500, 2.4, "Abeta(1-42)", 10000, 2.55
)
trough_long <- sim_trough |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment, cren_nM = Cc_nM,
                   `Abeta(1-40)` = Ctotal_ab40 / 1000,
                   `Abeta(1-42)` = Ctotal_ab42 / 1000) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Abeta(1-40)`, `Abeta(1-42)`), names_to = "species", values_to = "ab_nM")
breaks <- c(0, 500, 1500, 2500, 3500, 5000, 6500, 8500, Inf)
binned <- trough_long |>
  dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(cren_nM, breaks)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(species, bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cren_nM = median(cren_nM), med = median(ab_nM),
                   lo = quantile(ab_nM, 0.05), hi = quantile(ab_nM, 0.95),
                   n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(trough_long, aes(cren_nM, ab_nM)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = treatment), alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(data = binned, aes(x = cren_nM, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "purple", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = binned, aes(cren_nM, med)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4_line, shape = 4, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~species, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 10500)) +
  labs(x = "Crenezumab trough (nM)", y = "Total Abeta trough (nM)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper notes that, at steady-state trough for 60 mg/kg, crenezumab exceeds
plasma Abeta about 150-fold. For the typical patient at steady state:

```{r ratio}
ev_ss60 <- make_events(typical_cov, dose_mgkg = 60, dose_times = seq(0, 532, by = 28),
                       obs_times = 560 - 1e-3)
ss60 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev_ss60) |> as.data.frame()
ratio_60 <- ss60$Cc_nM / (ss60$Ctotal_ab40 / 1000)
ratio_60
stopifnot(ratio_60 > 120, ratio_60 < 190)
```

The plateau is a closed-form property of the Michaelis-Menten approximation.
As crenezumab rises, total Abeta approaches `baseline * Kdeg / kint`:
`r round(142 * 114 / (1.01/2.89) / 1000, 1)` nM for Abeta(1-40) and
`r round(5.98 * 287 / (1.01/2.89) / 1000, 2)` nM for Abeta(1-42). At the
highest Figure 4 troughs (7500-10000 nM) the free fraction is still about
0.1-0.2%, so the curves level off near 29 and 2.5 nM, below these limits.

```{r fig4-check}
# Binned simulated medians against the digitised published median line,
# interpolated at each bin's median crenezumab trough.
fig4_cmp <- binned |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 20, cren_nM >= 1000, cren_nM <= 10000) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(fig4 = approx(fig4_line$cren_nM[fig4_line$species == species],
                              fig4_line$ab_nM[fig4_line$species == species],
                              xout = cren_nM)$y) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (med / fig4 - 1))
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute("Species" = species, "Crenezumab trough (nM)" = round(cren_nM),
                   "Simulated median (nM)" = signif(med, 3),
                   "Figure 4 line (nM)" = signif(fig4, 3),
                   "Difference (%)" = round(pct_diff), "N" = n) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(
  abs(median(fig4_cmp$pct_diff[fig4_cmp$species == "Abeta(1-40)"])) < 20,
  abs(median(fig4_cmp$pct_diff[fig4_cmp$species == "Abeta(1-42)"])) < 20
)
```

# Free vs bound Abeta across doses (Figure 8)

Figure 8 simulates 6-480 mg/kg q4w for 140 days. Crenezumab is almost
entirely free. Plasma Abeta is almost entirely bound, so its total levels off
with dose while free Abeta keeps falling.

```{r fig8, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 8 of Yoshida 2020 (lower panels): typical-patient total (solid) and free (dashed) plasma Abeta for 6-480 mg/kg IV q4w."}
doses8 <- c(6, 15, 30, 45, 60, 120, 240, 480)
ev8 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses8), function(i) {
  make_events(typical_cov, dose_mgkg = doses8[i], dose_times = c(0, 28, 56, 84),
              obs_times = seq(0, 140, by = 0.5), id_offset = i - 1L) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = doses8[i])
}))
sim8 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, ev8, keep = "dose") |> as.data.frame()
sim8_long <- sim8 |>
  dplyr::transmute(dose, time,
                   `Abeta(1-40) total` = Ctotal_ab40 / 1000, `Abeta(1-40) free` = Cfree_ab40 / 1000,
                   `Abeta(1-42) total` = Ctotal_ab42 / 1000, `Abeta(1-42) free` = Cfree_ab42 / 1000) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(dose, time), names_to = c("species", "measure"),
                      names_sep = " (?=[a-z]+$)", values_to = "nM")
ggplot(sim8_long, aes(time, nM, colour = factor(dose), linetype = measure)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~species) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Plasma concentration (nM)", colour = "mg/kg", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

trough140 <- sim8 |> dplyr::filter(time == 140)
trough140 |>
  dplyr::transmute("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose,
                   "Total Abeta(1-40) (nM)" = signif(Ctotal_ab40 / 1000, 3),
                   "Free Abeta(1-40) (pM)" = signif(Cfree_ab40, 3),
                   "Free / baseline (%)" = signif(100 * Cfree_ab40 / 142, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Fold change in day-140 trough per doubling of dose, 60 -> 120 -> 240 -> 480.
dbl <- trough140 |>
  dplyr::filter(dose %in% c(60, 120, 240, 480)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total_fold = Ctotal_ab40 / dplyr::lag(Ctotal_ab40),
                free_fold = Cfree_ab40 / dplyr::lag(Cfree_ab40)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(total_fold))
dbl |>
  dplyr::transmute("Dose doubled to (mg/kg)" = dose,
                   "Total Abeta(1-40) fold change" = round(total_fold, 2),
                   "Free Abeta(1-40) fold change" = round(free_fold, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable()
# Deterministic typical-value solve: each doubling adds less total Abeta than
# the one before, and at the top doubling the fall in free Abeta is larger
# than the rise in total.
stopifnot(
  all(diff(dbl$total_fold) < 0),
  all(dbl$free_fold < 1),
  (1 - dbl$free_fold[3]) > (dbl$total_fold[3] - 1)
)
```

Each doubling of the dose adds less total Abeta than the previous one, while
free Abeta keeps falling by a similar or larger fraction. This is the
divergence between total and free Abeta that the paper's Discussion describes.

# PKNCA: steady-state crenezumab exposure at 60 mg/kg q4w (Figure 7, left column)

Figure 7 gives the typical patient's crenezumab AUC (about 183 uM*day) and Cmax
(about 13.0 uM) at 60 mg/kg. The 5th-95th percentile ranges across the
population are 139-238 uM*day and 9.6-16.8 uM. The Cmax matches steady state
(single-dose Cmax is 10 uM), so the comparison uses the 20th dosing interval of
a 200-patient cohort. The values were digitised from Figure 7 by the
maintainers.

```{r pknca}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200122)
ss_times <- c(532 + c(0, 1 / 24, 2 / 24, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 14, 21, 28))
ev_nca <- make_events(make_cov(200), dose_mgkg = 60, dose_times = seq(0, 532, by = 28),
                      obs_times = ss_times, id_offset = 1000L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "60 mg/kg q4w")
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_nca, keep = "treatment") |> as.data.frame()

conc_nca <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, treatment, time, Cc = Cc_nM / 1000)  # uM
dose_nca <- ev_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 532) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 532, end = 560, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "60 mg/kg q4w",  13.0,    183
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_sim,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "uM", auclast = "uM*day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable()

pct <- nca_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), median = median(PPORRES),
                   p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pct, digits = 1)

med_auc <- pct$median[pct$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
med_cmax <- pct$median[pct$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]
stopifnot(abs(med_auc / 183 - 1) < 0.1, abs(med_cmax / 13.0 - 1) < 0.1)
```

The simulated medians are within a few percent of the Figure 7 typical values,
and the simulated 5-95% ranges are close to the published ranges. The steady
state AUCtau is slightly below `Dose / CLel` because target-mediated
elimination of the bound complex removes about 2-3% of each dose at 60 mg/kg.

On the weight effect in Figure 7: with mg/kg dosing and the Table 2 exponents,
exposure scales as `WT^(1 - 0.835)` for AUC and `WT^(1 - 0.725)` for Cmax. That
predicts the 1.1-fold AUC and Cmax spread over 52.4-95.9 kg that the paper
reports. The paper's figure and text place the higher exposure at the lower
body weight, the opposite of what these exponents give for weight-based dosing.
The magnitude matches exactly, so the direction labels in Figure 7 appear to be
reversed.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Abeta central volume.** The paper gives Abeta peripheral volumes and
  intercompartmental clearances but no Abeta central volume. The model uses the
  crenezumab central volume Vcent, following the single-central-volume
  Michaelis-Menten TMDD form of the tutorial the paper cites (Dua 2015). This
  reading reproduces the Discussion's complex elimination rate
  (`CLint / Vcent` = 0.35 vs 0.36 /day) and the Figure 4 plateaus.
* **What distributes to the Abeta peripheral compartment.** The paper's Figure 1
  shows an Abeta peripheral compartment without saying whether free or total
  Abeta exchanges with it. The model distributes the total pool, with no drug
  binding or elimination in the periphery. The maintainers simulated both
  readings and compared them with Figure 3. For Abeta(1-40), distributing total
  Abeta gives day-7/day-1 ratios of 1.9 and 3.4 at 15 and 120 mg/kg, against
  1.9 and 3.8 published. Distributing free Abeta gives a much faster first-day
  rise, with ratios of 1.2 and 2.5. For Abeta(1-42) the total-distribution
  reading rises somewhat too slowly on day 1 (see the Figure 3 table), and the
  free-distribution reading rises far too fast. Both readings give the same
  steady state.
* **Crenezumab molecular weight.** Not printed. The binding terms need
  crenezumab in nM (Kd is in nM), and the drug-side target-mediated loss needs
  mass per pmol, so a nominal IgG MW of 150000 g/mol is used (`mw`). A
  different MW within 145-150 kDa shifts the PK exposures above by up to about
  3%.
* **Covariate reference values.** The paper does not state its centering
  values. The model uses the typical patient of Figure 7 (72.3 kg, 72 years,
  GFR 72.5 mL/min/1.73 m^2). At those values Figure 7 reproduces the Table 2
  baselines of 142 and 5.98 pM exactly. The body-weight effect is a power
  function `(WT / 72.3)^e`. The age, GFR and sex effects are linear,
  `(1 + e * (x - ref))`, and are multiplied together (Table 2 footnote).
* **Sex effect.** Table 2 reports a male effect of -0.16 on Kdeg, shared by
  both species. It is applied as `1 + e_sex_kdeg * (1 - SEXF)`, with female as
  the reference.
* **GFR.** Encoded as the `CRCL` column (BSA-normalized, mL/min/1.73 m^2). The
  paper does not state which estimating equation was used.
* **Shared random effects.** Table 2 footnote a states that the same BSV was
  used for Kd of both species and for Kdeg of both species. The model reads
  this as one eta per parameter pair (`etalkd`, `etalkdeg`), by analogy with
  footnote b, where one coefficient is shared.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports BSV as CV%. The variances use
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The paper does not say whether its percentages
  are true CVs or `100 * omega`. The two readings differ materially only for
  crenezumab Vperiph (75.2%: 0.448 vs 0.566).
* **Residual error.** Not reported in the paper. All three outputs carry a
  proportional error fixed to 0, so stochastic simulations show between-subject
  variability only.
* **Figure axis units.** Figure 2 is labelled ng/mL but plots ug/mL. Figure
  3's absolute values (labelled ng/mL) disagree about two-fold with Figure 4
  and Table 2, so only its shape was used.
* **Virtual cohort.** The paper reports no demographics table. Covariate
  distributions were built from the 90% ranges in the Results and Figure 7.
  The sex split (50%) is assumed.
* **CSF.** CSF crenezumab (about 0.3% of serum) and CSF Abeta(1-42) were
  analysed descriptively in the paper and are not part of the model.
